title: Scatter-Gather KV Coherence Playbook (draft)
content:
Summary:
This is a working playbook for a scatter-gather approach to KV cache coherence and placement across multi-GPU serving clusters. Focus is on practical heuristics for tensor/pipeline parallel workloads, NCCL tuning recipes for short collective-pairs, and an operational rollout plan. Goal: reduce tail latency and token cost by keeping per-request KV hits local where possible, while maintaining correctness and graceful degradation when cross-node collectives are expensive or unavailable.

Motivation & context:
- We see increased latency variance when models use pipeline + tensor parallel combos and KV sizes grow (>30GB across nodes).
- Naive global KV broadcast/replication either wastes memory or causes costly allgathers.
- Existing ring/allreduce NCCL defaults are tuned for large contiguous transfers; our common-case patterns are many small KV touches during early decoding and periodic prefetch/warmups.
- Need an operationally simple strategy compatible with Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals:
- Keep hot KV prefixes local to the GPU/node handling the request.
- Provide fallbacks that avoid full synchronous cross-node collectives on tail-sensitive requests.
- Provide NCCL and network tuning guidance for small-message collectives and microbatching that improves throughput without increasing P95 latency.
- Offer a migration and canary plan for rolling out new coherence logic in production clusters.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Fleet is heterogeneous: some nodes have NVLink, others rely on RDMA over InfiniBand, and some are single-GPU instances for Dedicated customers.
- Models use a mix of tensor and pipeline parallelism; tensor-parallel-only placements are simpler, but mixed placements require careful KV routing.
- We cannot assume unlimited GPU memory; caching must include eviction and spill-to-host policies.

High-level design (scatter-gather KV coherence):
1) Shard ownership + bloom filters:
   - Each KV shard has a stable primary owner (node) based on model-partitioning topology.
   - Each owner publishes a compact bloom filter of active prefixes (hot tokens/prefix hashes) at configurable intervals (10–200ms).
   - Request router consults the bloom filters to decide whether to route request to owner or serve locally with a miss.

2) Scatter path (write/update):
   - Writes (new cache population after generation) are first recorded locally and tagged as "pending propagation."
   - Propagation uses an async delta pipeline: owners apply local writes immediately, and every T_propagate (default 300ms) we aggregate deltas and push to secondaries via batched NCCL/allgather when beneficial, or via RDMA if available.

3) Gather path (read/lookup):
   - Lookup first consults local shard. On miss, consult in-memory bloom filters to pick candidate owners (top-1 or top-2).
   - If candidate owner is local node -> fetch direct. If remote, attempt remote RPC + async prefetch. For tail-sensitive requests (latency SLO < 50ms), we fallback to approximate answer using partial KV (local-only), while logging telemetry and optionally re-issuing a low-priority background request to refresh cache.

4) Eviction & spill:
   - LRU-like policy with prefix-weighting: prefixes with high re-use score are kept. When eviction moves entries out of GPU memory, we spill compressed quantized KV to host-SSD.

NCCL and networking tuning guidance (recipes):
- Small-collectives pattern (many small KV deltas):
  * Use NCCL P2P for intra-node when NVLink present (enable NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL).
  * For cross-node small allgathers, prefer using explicit batched transfers over many small NCCL ops. Group small deltas into coarse-grained buffers (4–16KB -> 64–256KB grouping) before issuing the collective.
  * Tune NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_BUFFSIZE to allow more outstanding operations when grouping.
  * For IB-backed clusters, ensure HCA drivers are tuned for small-message performance (increase max_inline_recv/resp settings).

- Large-model checkpoint syncs (periodic):
  * Use tuned tree-based collectives (non-ring) for large, contiguous checkpoints. NCCL_COLLNET may also be evaluated on homogenous IB clusters.

Microbatching + scheduling heuristics:
- Use adaptive microbatching: start with low microbatch size for first N tokens (latency sensitive), then increase batch window for steady-state generation to improve throughput.
- Scheduler should be topology-aware: co-locate requests with similar KV shard affinity into the same execution epoll window so we can amortize remote fetches and kernel footprint.
- Provide a credit-based admission controller that prevents request storms from overwhelming remote owners (credits available per owner based on recent service latency).

Prefetch strategy and proactive warming:
- For chat sessions, prefetch likely next-token KV on hypothesis scoring (beam / candidate generation) boundaries.
- Proactive warming jobs run at low priority: scan logs for popular prefixes (daily) and seed owners' GPU caches before business hours.

Correctness and consistency model:
- We expose eventual consistency for KV reads with three knobs a customer can choose per route: strong (synchronous), bounded (sync within X ms), best-effort (local-first with async propagation). Default for Hosted and Dedicated is bounded with X=300ms.
- Strong mode will route read/write to owner and block until confirmation — expensive, intended for sensitive workloads.

Metrics and telemetry to collect:
- Per-route: local-KV-hit-rate, remote-KV-latency (P50/P95/P99), propagation-lag histogram, eviction-rate, spill-rate to host-SSD, NCCL-small-collective-latency, grouped-delta-size distribution.
- Failure signals: async-propagation-drop-rate, owner-throttle-events, bloom-filter-fpr (false positive rate).

Experiment matrix (recommended tests):
- A/B: current global-replicated KV vs scatter-gather bounded (X=300ms) on identical traffic, measure P50/P95 token latency and GPU memory usage.
- NCCL grouping: compare raw small-collectives vs grouped-batched transfers (vary grouping size 4KB..256KB).
- Topology skew: test mix of NVLink vs RDMA-only nodes to validate routing heuristics.
- Fault injection: kill owner node mid-session and observe fallback correctness and recovery latencies.

Operational rollout plan (canary -> ramp):
1) Internal dev clusters: enable best-effort mode, run long-running load tests with synthetic and replayed traffic.
2) Small canary on Dedicated fleet: select 2 pods per region with adaptive prefetch disabled, monitor metrics for 72h.
3) Open beta for select Hosted customers (opt-in), enable bounded mode X=500ms.
4) After observed stable metrics, reduce X to 300ms and ramp to 50% of traffic.
5) Full rollout with default bounded mode if no regressions.

Safety nets & fallbacks:
- If remote RPC latency spikes beyond threshold, scheduler marks owner as degraded and temporarily increases local-only serving percentage.
- Automatic rollback on Canary: if P95 tokens increase by >10% or error-rate > 2x baseline for 1h, revert routing to global replica path.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Best compact filter format for large prefix spaces (bloom vs cuckoo vs counting filters) — run memory/CPU tradeoff bench.
- Optimal grouping window for small NCCL collectives under 100 microsecond latencies — needs cluster-specific microbenchmarks.
- How to integrate with per-customer placement constraints in Private deployments (air-gapped networks).

Action items (short term):
- [Jordan] run bloom vs cuckoo microbench on representative prefix corpus (due 2024-11-22).
- [Maya] prototype grouped-delta buffer and measure small-collective latency reduction (due 2024-12-06).
- [Carlos] add lambda in telemetry to compute per-prefix hotness and export to Console (due 2024-12-15).
- [Eun-ji] draft canary checklist and rollback playbook for SRE (due 2024-12-20).

Appendix: quick NCCL env knobs we found helpful in experiments:
- NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0 (default) for heterogeneous clusters, enable only when your network is stable and homogeneous.
- NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL or SYS depending on whether NVLink present.
- NCCL_BUFFSIZE=1048576 (tune up for batched grouping workloads).
- NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 to avoid hangs during transient errors.
- Export ML_COMM_BACKEND=nccl, fall back to grpc/rdma for small control plane events.

Notes on documentation & next steps:
- Convert this playbook into an internal runbook and link to Console alerts (KV-hit-rate < 70%).
- Create GitHub epic to track experiments and PRs for the grouped-delta implementation.
- Schedule a cross-team sync with Platform Placement team to align owner selection heuristics with upcoming Dedicated placement API changes.

End of draft.

(Free-form notes to self)
- Might be worth evaluating CRDT-style deltas for extremely high churn prefixes, but complexity is high and probably unnecessary for most workloads.
- Consider exposing per-customer consistency knob in the API to unblock regulated customers who need stronger guarantees.
